title: 3M Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates as Company Raises Full-Year Guidance
excerpt: 3M posts adjusted EPS of $2.50 on $6.58 billion in sales and lifts its 2026 outlook.
body:
3M reported third-quarter results on October 20, 2026 that came in ahead of Wall Street expectations on profit, as the industrial conglomerate's turnaround continued to gain traction. Adjusted earnings per share rose 12 percent year over year to $2.50, beating the consensus estimate of about $2.40, while GAAP earnings per share reached $2.63. Sales totaled $6.58 billion, up 4.2 percent on an adjusted basis with organic growth of 3.3 percent, landing just shy of the $6.61 billion analysts had forecast.

Profitability improved again in the quarter. The adjusted operating margin expanded 110 basis points to 26.2 percent, reflecting productivity gains and pricing discipline across the portfolio. Adjusted free cash flow was $1.2 billion, and the company returned $0.6 billion to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases during the quarter.

Safety and Industrial was the standout segment, with sales up 9.1 percent to $3.18 billion on continued demand for protective equipment and industrial adhesives. Transportation and Electronics and the Consumer business were more mixed, with softer demand in some end markets partly offsetting the industrial strength.

Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $9.10 to $9.15, its second increase this year, and pointed to a growing data-center opportunity: 3M expanded its optical-connectivity relationship with Amazon, including a warrant tied to future sales milestones. Investors welcomed the report, sending the shares up about 5 percent on the day.
